instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and lightly grease a baking dish.
Dice the onion. Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large skillet over medium. Add the beef and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, breaking it into small pieces, until it's browned.
Add the onion and cook for 4 minutes, until it's soft.
Add the chili powder, paprika, garlic powder, cumin, oregano and salt. Stir for 1 minute, until you can smell them. Taste the beef and add a pinch more salt if it's flat. Take the pan off the heat.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or the microwave for about 20 seconds, so they roll without cracking.
Spread a quarter of the refried beans over the lower middle of each tortilla and top with a quarter of the beef. Fold in the sides, then roll it up tightly from the bottom.
Place them seam side down in the baking dish and brush the tops with the remaining 1 tbsp oil.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the tortillas are crisp and golden.
Slice the avocados. Serve the chimichangas with the salsa and the avocado.

To store, let the baked chimichangas cool completely, then keep them in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 5 days or in the freezer for up to 3 months. To reheat from the fridge, bake them at 400°F for 10 minutes. From the freezer, thaw them overnight in the fridge, then bake at 400°F for about 20 minutes, until hot in the middle.
method_notes: The Urben Life browns the beef with onion and a chili, paprika, cumin and oregano mix, spreads refried beans on burrito tortillas, rolls them and bakes at 425°F until crisp, which this follows. Heart's Content Farmhouse adds black beans and cheese and freezes them unbaked, wrapped in foil. Six Sisters' Stuff bakes them at a lower heat for 30 to 35 minutes with melted butter on top. This keeps the lead's mild filling with no cheese.
